decisions.reason: The AXP2101 requirement already covers all system loads and both required rails; adding a backlight load to the downstream 5V boost rail does not change its power-path state.
The current backlight build uses the 5V rail, while the unpopulated 3.3V jumper is only a future fallback; DCDC1 regulation and its existing 3.3V loads remain unchanged.

This Requirement already has a same-message MODIFY that fully records the backlight supply, switching circuit, fallback option, and approximately 70mA load; no additional or corrected update is needed.
The 5V rail is already monitored as a whole, so adding another load to that rail does not change the monitoring device, monitored rails, channel allocation, or measurement topology.
The external e-paper backlight is independent of the battery-charge status LED interfaces and does not alter their connectors, signals, resistance, or population rules.
The backlight circuit does not change the panel power-button connector, PWRON connection, board location, or press behavior.
Adding an approximately 70mA downstream 5V backlight load does not entail any change to the specified AXP2101 exposed-pad thermal assembly requirement.
The backlight supply and switching specification does not affect the battery connector family, pitch, pin count, functions, part number, or unresolved pin order.
The source specifies a downstream backlight load but does not change battery protection control, cutoff voltages, or DW01A protection details.
The external backlight does not change the battery NTC terminal, connector, monitoring function, or thermal-protection controller.
J_DISP_LED is a display-backlight interface, not a sensor-module or interboard connector, so the sensor fanout remains valid unchanged.
The populated configuration powers the backlight from 5V; the unpopulated 3.3V jumper is only a future fallback and does not establish a new load or behavior for standalone USB 3.3V operation.
